structured_conclusion.macro_trend: Disinflationary Slowdown (US) Overlaid by a China DUV Chip-Tool Shock to Korea/AI-Memory Semis
structured_conclusion.likely_rotation: Broad US market (SPY, credit, duration) largely absorbing today's move; capital actively rotating out of Korea/memory semis (EWY, SOXX, DRAM, SK Hynix, Samsung) into defensives/mega-cap
structured_conclusion.next_catalyst: SK Hynix Q2 earnings (today/tomorrow) + FOMC decision Jul 28-29, both within 48h, compounded by an unresolved China DUV chip-tool shock
structured_conclusion.korea_gate: Closed 1/3 -- USDKRW pass only; EWY $152.05 vs SMA20 $174.43 (gap widened sharply to -12.8%); KOSPI 6,023.67 (-10.84%, worst single-day drop in years, still far below 8,200)

bias: Broad US financial conditions read constructive on their own terms today -- oil fell a second straight sharp session (-4.47%, on top of Jul27's -7.37%), both 5Y and 10Y breakevens fell together, credit proxies ALLY/CACC/COF all bounced in unison for the first time in days, and VIX pulled back. Taken alone that's a genuine easing-at-the-margin story, not just 'liquidity tightening.' But that read is almost beside the point today: South Korea's KOSPI just had its steepest single-day drop in years (-10.84%, repeated trading halts), with SK Hynix -14.65% and Samsung -13.39%, after news that China has begun mass production of homegrown DUV lithography tools -- a structural competitiveness shock to the AI-memory trade, not a financial-conditions story. SOXX (-5.03%) and DRAM (-9.01%) show early US spillover, while SPY (+0.22%) and QQQ (-0.94%) have so far absorbed it without panic, and US credit/vol are not confirming stress. The open question is whether SK Hynix's own earnings (expected record profit) and the FOMC, both landing in the same 48-hour window, stabilize sentiment or compound it.

counterargs.thesis: Disinflationary Slowdown with contained US credit/vol, but a live, unresolved China-competition shock to Korea/AI-memory semis
supporting: Oil -4.47% to $78.92, second straight sharp down day
T5YIE/T10YIE breakevens both fell (-6bps/-5bps) -- broad disinflation signal, not just short-end noise
ALLY (+1.14%), CACC (+1.03%), COF (+1.66%) all bounced together -- first synchronized credit-proxy bounce in days
USDKRW still comfortably below the 1,530 BOK line despite the KOSPI crash -- no FX contagion yet
against: KOSPI -10.84%, worst single-day drop in years, trading halted multiple times
SK Hynix -14.65%, Samsung -13.39% on China DUV chip-tool mass-production news -- a structural, not sentiment-driven, catalyst
SOXX -5.03%, DRAM -9.01%; SOXX/SPY ratio (0.662) at a fresh cycle low
KOSPI down roughly 34% in 25 sessions after a 297% run -- deleveraging risk not obviously exhausted
FOMC decision and SK Hynix's own earnings both land within 48h, stacking binary risk on top of an already-live shock
counterargs.read: The US-centric dashboard -- oil, breakevens, credit proxies, VIX -- reads genuinely better today, and that's real. But it's largely orthogonal to what's actually moving markets: a structural competitive shock to Korea's AI-memory trade from China's DUV tooling breakthrough, landing on top of a KOSPI that had already round-tripped much of a historic 297% run. SOXX and DRAM show the US semis complex is not fully insulated, even as SPY and QQQ have absorbed the shock calmly so far. Whether SK Hynix's own earnings (expected record profit) can arrest the slide, or the market treats them as irrelevant next to a structural re-rating of Korea's competitive position, is the swing factor -- and it resolves in the same window as the FOMC.
